user_scenario:
You are Tessa Lindqvist, a Full-Service shopper in Austin who has been shopping for Cartwise for about two and a half years. You are calling Cartwise shopper support on a weekday afternoon between batches; you are a little irritated but practical and you keep your answers short. The reason you are calling: the store manager at Whole Foods on Lamar complained about you on September 15 and it landed on your account as a conduct complaint, and you want to dispute the conduct complaint. The store kept you waiting at the pickup counter for close to half an hour, you asked twice when the order would be ready, and the manager wrote you up as rude, which you were not. You want the points that should not be there taken off. You do not know how many points that violation carries or how a dispute is worked out, and you want support to tell you what it comes to. You know a dispute is something you file yourself, so when the agent sets the dispute up in your app and tells you what to enter, you file it yourself right then, using exactly the account, the violation reference and the number of points the agent gives you; you do not file anything before the agent hands it to you.

When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your mobile number 5125534817 first, and if they want a second detail you give your email tessa.lindqvist@mailvista.com. You do not volunteer anything else about yourself; only if the agent asks for them, your date of birth is 1991-03-14 and your home ZIP code is 78704. If the agent asks which batch or order you mean, you say it was the double batch from Whole Foods on Lamar on September 15, the evening one with two orders. If they ask what happened, you describe the wait at the counter and asking twice about the order; you have no screenshots or witnesses.

If the agent explains that something else on your account has to be booked or settled before your dispute can be worked out, you say something like "Okay, if that's how it works, go ahead and take care of it" and you let them do it without arguing. Only if the agent brings up a Stock-Up batch you dropped in September do you say that you released it yourself the morning after you took it, because your plans changed, and you know that one was on you. Only if the agent brings up an order from your triple batch that was marked as not delivered do you say you remember the pay being taken back on that one and you are not going to argue it. If the agent asks whether you have any other disputes open, you say you do not keep track and they can see whatever is on your account.

You do not know Cartwise's rules or the right figure, and you never suggest a number of points yourself. When the agent tells you the number of points to enter for your dispute, you accept it and use it when you file. Once you have filed and the agent tells you the dispute went through, you thank them and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The missing-items decision is parallel to the chain dropped-batch -> wrong-address. It books a cleared entry, and neither severity reads cleared entries (the dropped-batch severity counts recorded violations of the last month, the wrong-address severity recorded violations of the last three months, base-pay rows, the batch ratings, the activation date and the recorded wrong-address count), while the missing-items excusal reads the submitted dispute, its violation, its batch, the order rating and the count of recorded missing-items violations, none of which the two recordings change (they record batch_dropped and wrong_address). Replaying the orders [missing, dropped, wrong-address, conduct] and [dropped, wrong-address, missing, conduct] gives 1, 4, 5, 3 in both and the same terminal rows. The dropped-batch severity must precede the wrong-address severity: the latter's rule states it is fixed only after every dropped batch carries its entry (booked the other way the wrong-address count would be 4 and its points 4).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the missing-items decision the other standing points are 11 (>= standing_high_points 11), the standing-points reduction is 2 and the conduct-complaint dispute removes 2 points instead of 3; the dispute also stays submitted and its point stays on the 2026-09-14 violation.

Without the wrong-address booking the other standing points are 5 (< standing_mid_points 6), the reduction is 0 and the dispute removes 4 points instead of 3; the owed wrong_address entry is also missing from the terminal ledger.

Without the dropped-batch booking the wrong-address severity sees 4 recorded violations in three months (track surcharge 1) and books 4 points instead of 5; the batch_dropped entry is also missing, and the root then removes 4 instead of 3.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 0 (shopper_ratings_and_deactivations, category shopper). frozen_time 2026-09-22 15:10:00 CDT.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Tessa Lindqvist (Full-Service Shopper Diamond, account 4f80ffc6-6b29-40f8-9cb5-39879a35274f) asks for one thing: to dispute the
store conduct complaint booked on 2026-09-15 (4 points). The points she gets back (3) are a five-factor excusal (counter wait
beyond the batch type's free minutes, the 5-star praise count of the last month, a tenure method on that sum, a
prior-complaint reduction and a standing-points reduction over every other recorded-minus-cleared point). The standing input
is only right after three problems she never mentions: a missing-items dispute still standing submitted (the agent decides
it, -1), an owed wrong-address violation behind a batch-pay reversal (the agent books it, +5) and, behind that, an owed
dropped-batch violation for a shopper_choice drop (+4) that the wrong-address severity's three-month track tier counts.

2. SCOPE. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5, 6, 4, 6]; allocation: dropped-batch
severity 6, wrong-address severity 6, conduct-complaint excusal 5 (root), missing-items excusal 4. Task 1 holds the
dropped-batch, wrong-address, alcohol-procedure and late-delivery excusals; scopes are disjoint and cover all eight policies.
Severity is booked only for owed violations whose evidence sits on the shopper's own records (a shopper_choice drop; a
not-delivered pay reversal); every other type is only disputed.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: shopper_ext_conduct_complaint_excusal (dispute_conduct_complaint_violation_2203c191, owner=user).
 Edge A: root <- shopper_ext_missing_items_excusal, value_input, gate other_standing_points, state form: "The points a
 conduct-complaint dispute removes are not fixed until no missing-items dispute on the account stands submitted and
 undecided." False: shopper_appeals.9b2eaae8-41c9-4e91-ba38-349868225cfa.appeal_status = submitted (source c347065a-1320-451f-a625-8aed832b8965). Resolved by
 decide_missing_items_dispute_36c35ef8, the only write that decides a submitted missing-items dispute. Deletion run: 3 -> 2.
 Edge B: root <- shopper_ext_wrong_address_severity, value_input, gate other_standing_points, state form: "The points a
 conduct-complaint dispute removes are fixed only after every batch pay taken back for an order verified as not delivered is
 matched by its wrong-address violation entry." False: batch_events.8d2fbaf6-48c4-4e79-ab45-329c042d585f (2026-09-20, 3.00, order_not_delivered_verified)
 has no wrong_address entry on batch c8cc347e-2e6d-4f1c-b608-124a9e503489 (the January reversal is matched by the 2026-01-20 violation). Resolved by
 record_wrong_address_violation_db63d782. Deletion run: 3 -> 4.
 Edge C: wrong-address severity <- shopper_ext_dropped_batch_severity, value_input, gate recent_three_month_violations, state
 form: "The points a wrong-address violation is booked with are fixed only after every batch the account dropped by its own
 choice carries its dropped-batch violation entry." False: batches.739be8c3-0486-457a-a6b9-47407e4ce7db status dropped, drop_reason shopper_choice
 (2026-09-12), no batch_dropped entry. Resolved by record_dropped_batch_violation_61b8c422. Deletion run: wrong-address 5 -> 4,
 root 3 -> 4. Only shopper_choice drops owe a violation, in step with the batch charter (a drop whose reason is in
 excused_drop_reasons records none; the batch_dropped trigger fires only for shopper_choice).
 Four-point test per sentence: ordering connective (not ... until / only after); record-visible state in finder words; no
 tool, id or code token; hard requirement over "every"/"no". One negated, two affirmative. Topological order: missing ->
 dropped -> wrong-address -> conduct (gold steps 8, 10, 12, 14); the missing-items decision commutes with the chain
 (order_uniqueness: 1, 4, 5, 3 either way). user_scenario names none of the three; tools validate nothing.

4. FACTOR CARD (handling-time sensitivity; figure = result with that factor at its baseline).
 missing-items excusal = 1 (recorded 2): 50 units -> 1 (base -> 0); Stock-Up doubles -> 2 (as-is -> 0); latest rating 4 stars
 -> 1 (base -> 0); two other missing-items violations in three months -> 2 (base -> 2 capped); all-baseline 0.
 dropped-batch severity = 4: started single order -> 1 (base -> 2; multi-source); Stock-Up +half up -> 2 (as-is -> 3); 2
 violations in the last month -> 1 (base -> 3); held 1 day -> 1 (base -> 3); 45 stranded units -> 1 (base -> 3); 11 paid
 batches -> relief 3 (base -> 7); all-baseline 2. Cross-difficulty batch.
 wrong-address severity = 5: three-order batch -> 1 (base -> 7); 3.00 clawback -> 1 (base -> 4); 5 violations in three months
 incl. today's dropped-batch entry -> 2 (base -> 3); a 2-star (no 1-star) rating on the batch -> 1 (base -> 4); one earlier
 wrong-address violation in twelve months -> 1 (base -> 4); tenure 946 days -> 1 (base -> 6); all-baseline 3.
 conduct-complaint excusal = 3 (recorded 4): excess wait 12 -> 1 (base -> 1); 9 five-star ratings -> 2 (base -> 0); tenure +half
 up 3 -> 5 (as-is -> 1); one other complaint (2026-04-20) -> 1 (base -> 4); other standing 10 -> 1 (base -> 4); all-baseline 0.
 Near-misses: the 2026-08-10 violation lies outside one whole month for the dropped-batch track tier; the expired April
 complaint and the expired January wrong-address violation still count as recorded in their twelve-month tiers.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. dispute_window (shopper_evt_violations, time): anchor the violation's event_date, not_after,
 violation_dispute_days (Diamond 14), day 0, inclusive, judged at submission. Missing-items violation 2026-09-14, dispute
 submitted 2026-09-16 (last day 2026-09-28); conduct complaint 2026-09-15 filed in-app 2026-09-22 (last day 2026-09-29).
 one_per_type_per_order is superseded clause by clause in both severities. Base points stay for conduct (4) and missing items (2).

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Decision: dispute 9b2eaae8-41c9-4e91-ba38-349868225cfa -> violation c347065a-1320-451f-a625-8aed832b8965. Dropped-batch: the only dropped batch 739be8c3-0486-457a-a6b9-47407e4ce7db, reason
 shopper_choice. Wrong-address: the unmatched reversal 8d2fbaf6-48c4-4e79-ab45-329c042d585f -> batch c8cc347e-2e6d-4f1c-b608-124a9e503489. Conduct dispute: the most recent conduct-complaint
 entry 3a6fa3f8-bf63-45a1-b810-b14a18d6622d. Clearings offset only their own source violations.

7. SEED. customers 1, shopper_accounts 1 (balance 6 = recorded 16 - cleared 10, below Diamond hold 13), shopper_events 26,
 shopper_appeals 3, batches 15, batch_events 49; no payout rows (no computation reads them). After all writes the ledger
 balance is 6 - 1 + 4 + 5 - 3 = 11 (< hold 13); the mid-call peak 14 stays under the Diamond deactivation threshold 16.
 Level note: Diamond since the 2026-07-01 change, kept within its demotion grace cycles; only the batches the reads need are seeded.

8. PERSONA. Short, practical; volunteers only the dispute and its story; credentials only when asked (phone, then email);
 reacts to the dropped batch ("released it yourself ... plans changed") or the not-delivered order only if raised; generic
 go-ahead for prerequisites; files the dispute herself with the figures given; ends on confirmation; no extra asks.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, email) -> find_shopper_accounts -> find_shopper_events ->
 find_shopper_appeals -> find_batches -> find_batch_events -> decide the missing-items dispute (1) -> record the dropped-batch
 violation (4) -> record the wrong-address violation (5) -> hand over the in-app dispute; the shopper files it (3).

10. VERIFICATION. check_extended / check_task_tools / replay_tasks / check_solvability / check_compute / check_grounding /
 check_cross_fire --task 0: all OK after round 2; the handling-time sensitivity run printed 1, 4, 5, 3 with the figures above
 and edge runs 3->2, 3->4, 5->4.

11. REVISIONS. Round 1: clawback thresholds; dispute date; no order rows; root changed to the conduct complaint. Round 2
 (audit): F1/T0-F1 the dropped-batch severity applies only to shopper_choice drops (fault ladder removed, stranded-items
 surcharge added, volume relief 3), the seeded drop is a shopper_choice drop with 45 units; F3/T0-F3 clawback relief replaced
 by the repeat-address surcharge, payout rows and reads removed, a January wrong-address violation seeded; level Diamond,
 conduct standing tiers 11/6; T0-F4 the appeals read's objective now dates the dispute 2026-09-16.
